prior_decision_preserved.decision_scope: connectomic structural retention only; not a learning-performance claim
prior_decision_preserved.interpretation: If a <=10k PPR core passes, the next round should instantiate that exact individual-neuron subgraph with shared type-level dynamics but independent neuron states. If only >10k cores pass, do not force the 10k target; inspect which network/semantic shells enter between 10k and the first passing budget. If no tested budget passes, expand the budget ladder or reconsider the seed/universe definitions before dynamics experiments.

next_action: Audit weak-edge and universe-boundary exclusions before revising the connectivity criterion. Increasing the node budget inside this same universe cannot satisfy the original 99% gate.
limits: Original 10k/15k memberships are fixed; no PPR reranking.
Weak connectivity ignores direction; directed degrees and strong components are also reported.
Seed-pair retention is an explanatory metric, not a replacement passing threshold.
External edges do not establish a path reconnecting a seed to the learning circuit.
Threshold sensitivity does not establish biological efficacy of weaker edges.
No cells are merged, seeds deleted, neural models trained, or learning performance inferred.
